13:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ Διδάσκαλε, ἴδε ποταποὶ λίθοι καὶ ποταπαὶ οἰκοδομαί.
13:1.targetText: And as He is going forth out of the temple, one of His disciples says to Him, “Teacher, see! What stones! And what buildings!”

groups.note: The genitive-absolute departure participle supplies the temporal as ... is going forth construction; there is no separately written Greek as conjunction.

13:2.sourceText: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Βλέπεις ταύτας τὰς μεγάλας οἰκοδομάς; οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ μὴ καταλυθῇ.
13:2.targetText: And Jesus answering said to him, “See these great buildings? There may not be left a stone on a stone that may not be thrown down.”

groups.note: Greek Βλέπεις is a present second-person seeing question, do you see; LSV shortens the question to See these buildings, retaining the actual seeing head.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The answering participle follows the longer TR reading and is absent from pinned N1904.

13:3.sourceText: Καὶ καθημένου αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν κατέναντι τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν Πέτρος καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάνης καὶ Ἀνδρέας
13:3.targetText: And as He is sitting at the Mount of Olives, opposite the temple, Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, were questioning Him by Himself,

groups.note: The genitive-absolute sitting participle supplies the temporal as ... is sitting construction, without a separately printed as word.
The written verb ἐπηρώτα is singular, with Peter leading the coordinated names; LSV uses English plural were questioning for the named group. The actual questioning head is retained.
The idiom κατ᾽ ἰδίαν means privately/apart; LSV by Himself expresses this private audience without a separate Greek reflexive pronoun.

13:4.sourceText: Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν, πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα συντελεῖσθαι πάντα;
13:4.targetText: “Tell us when these things will be? And what [is] the sign when all these may be about to be fulfilled?”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the Greek nominal what-the-sign question; there is no finite be verb there.

13:5.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἤρξατο λέγειν αὐτοῖς Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ.
13:5.targetText: And Jesus answering them, began to say, “Take heed lest anyone may lead you astray,

groups.note: The actual Greek dative speech recipients of began-to-say are the same people whom LSV places with answering; the audience is retained while the added answering predicate itself is separately unpaired.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV answering follows an added TR response participle; N1904 has only began to say to them.

13:6.sourceText: πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
13:6.targetText: for many will come in My Name, saying, I am [He], and many they will lead astray;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Greek ὅτι introduces the quotation; LSV directly prints I am without that.

unmappedTarget.reason: The initial for follows an added TR γάρ, absent from N1904.
Bracketed English He completes the identity claim I am; N1904 has no separately written third-person predicate pronoun.

13:7.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γενέσθαι, ἀλλ’ οὔπω τὸ τέλος.
13:7.targetText: and when you may hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be troubled, for these ought to be, but the end [is] not yet;

unmappedTarget.reason: The explanatory for and explicit these subject follow the longer TR reading; N1904 directly has it-is-necessary to happen without those words.
English supplies the copula in the Greek not-yet-the-end nominal clause.

13:8.sourceText: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν. ἔσονται σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους, ἔσονται λιμοί· ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων ταῦτα.
13:8.targetText: for nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles; these [are the] beginning of travails.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English connective before earthquakes follows extra TR connective wording; N1904 directly has there-will-be earthquakes.
The English connective before the second there-will-be clause is not separately written in N1904.
The additional troubles item with its conjunction follows the longer TR reading, absent from N1904.
Bracketed English copula/article supply the Greek nominal beginning-of-travails-these clause; no corresponding be verb or article is printed.

13:9.sourceText: Βλέπετε δὲ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτούς· παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς δαρήσεσθε καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων σταθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
13:9.targetText: And take heed to yourselves, for they will deliver you up to Sanhedrins, and to synagogues, you will be beaten, and before governors and kings you will be set for My sake, for a testimony to them;

groups.note: The explicit you plus reflexive yourselves intensifies the watched persons; LSV expresses both as the single yourselves phrase under take heed to.

unmappedTarget.reason: The explanatory for before deliver follows added TR γάρ; N1904 directly begins the delivery clause.

13:10.sourceText: καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πρῶτον δεῖ κηρυχθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
13:10.targetText: and to all the nations it is first necessary that the good news be proclaimed.

groups.note: The proclamation infinitive after necessary is recast as an English that-clause with good news as subject; that expresses the complement construction, not a separate Greek conjunction.

13:11.sourceText: καὶ ὅταν ἄγωσιν ὑμᾶς παραδιδόντες, μὴ προμεριμνᾶτε τί λαλήσητε, ἀλλ’ ὃ ἐὰν δοθῇ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ, τοῦτο λαλεῖτε· οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑμεῖς οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον.
13:11.targetText: And when they may lead you, delivering up, do not be anxious beforehand what you may speak, nor premeditate, but whatever may be given to you in that hour, that speak, for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The added premeditation prohibition follows the longer TR reading and is absent from pinned N1904.

13:12.sourceText: καὶ παραδώσει ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς·
13:12.targetText: And brother will deliver up brother to death, and father child, and children will rise up against parents, and will put them to death,

13:13.sourceText: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος, οὗτος σωθήσεται.
13:13.targetText: and you will be hated by all because of My Name, but he who has endured to the end—he will be saved.

13:14.sourceText: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως ἑστηκότα ὅπου οὐ δεῖ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη,
13:14.targetText: And when you may see the abomination of the desolation, that was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it should not (whoever is reading let him understand), then those in Judea, let them flee to the mountains;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.text: that was spoken of by Daniel the prophet
unmappedTarget.reason: The explicit Daniel-prophet attribution follows the longer TR reading and is absent from pinned N1904 at this verse.

13:15.sourceText: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω μηδὲ εἰσελθάτω τι ἆραι ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,
13:15.targetText: and he on the housetop, do not let him come down into the house, nor come in to take anything out of his house;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an initial coordinating and following TR καί; N1904 directly gives the housetop person.
The explicit house destination after come down follows TR wording and is absent from pinned N1904 there. The later actual house noun belongs to out of his house.

13:16.sourceText: καὶ ὁ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.
13:16.targetText: and he who is in the field, do not let him turn to the things behind, to take up his garment.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the nominal he-who-in-field phrase; Greek has no be verb or being participle.

13:17.sourceText: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
13:17.targetText: And woe to those with child, and to those giving suck, in those days;

groups.note: The actual Greek pregnancy idiom is having in the womb/stomach, ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις; LSV with child renders that complete state without inventing a separate Greek child noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

13:18.sourceText: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται χειμῶνος·
13:18.targetText: and pray that your flight may not be in winter,

unmappedTarget.reason: The explicit flight noun and possessor follow the longer TR reading; N1904 has the situation understood without these printed words.

13:19.sourceText: ἔσονται γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι θλῖψις, οἵα οὐ γέγονεν τοιαύτη ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἣν ἔκτισεν ὁ Θεὸς ἕως τοῦ νῦν καὶ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
13:19.targetText: for those days will be tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the creation that God created, until now, and may not be [again];

groups.note: The Greek correlative οἵα ... τοιαύτη, such as ... such, is compressed to the single English such as comparison; both actual comparative modifiers share that expression.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English again makes the future non-recurrence explicit; N1904 has the negative future-event construction without a separate again adverb.

13:20.sourceText: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολόβωσεν Κύριος τὰς ἡμέρας, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ· ἀλλὰ διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἐκολόβωσεν τὰς ἡμέρας.
13:20.targetText: and if the LORD did not shorten the days, no flesh had been saved; but because of the chosen, whom He chose to Himself, He shortened the days.

groups.note: Greek not ... all flesh would have been saved is rendered no flesh had been saved; the negative and universal jointly express that scope recast.

The modal particle ἄν with the past passive saving verb marks the unreal consequence of the if-not condition. LSV’s had been saved expresses that counterfactual result, not an ordinary past assertion.
The middle choosing predicate ἐξελέξατο is rendered He chose to Himself, making its self-involving election relation explicit without an independently printed Greek reflexive pronoun.

13:21.sourceText: καὶ τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ Ἴδε ὧδε ὁ Χριστός, Ἴδε ἐκεῖ, μὴ πιστεύετε·
13:21.targetText: And then, if any may say to you, Behold, here [is] the Christ, or, Behold, there, you may not believe;

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the nominal here-the-Christ designation; no finite be verb is printed.
LSV or follows extra TR ἤ between the here/there sayings; pinned N1904 directly repeats behold.

13:22.sourceText: ἐγερθήσονται δὲ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ ποιήσουσιν σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πρὸς τὸ ἀποπλανᾶν εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
13:22.targetText: for there will rise false Christs and false prophets, and they will give signs and wonders, to seduce, if possible, also the chosen;

groups.note: The N1904 connective δέ introduces the next warning; LSV for follows TR γάρ and makes its explanatory force explicit.
N1904 ποιήσουσιν means they will do/produce signs; LSV gives they will give signs, describing the same sign-producing event without inventing a Greek δίδωμι token.
The πρός plus nominalized seducing infinitive expresses the intended effect; English to seduce renders that complete purpose construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV also follows added TR καί before the chosen, absent from N1904.

13:23.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ βλέπετε· προείρηκα ὑμῖν πάντα.
13:23.targetText: and you, take heed; behold, I have foretold you all things.

unmappedTarget.reason: The extra behold follows TR ἰδού, absent from pinned N1904.

13:24.sourceText: Ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν ἐκείνην ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

13:25.sourceText: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες ἔσονται ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πίπτοντες, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς σαλευθήσονται.
13:25.targetText: and the stars of the sky will be falling, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

groups.note: N1904 places from the sky with falling; LSV attaches the sky as a source/association description of the stars, of the sky. The actual sky relation is retained with its changed clause attachment explicit, not a general from=of claim.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the powers-that-in-heavens article/prepositional modifier; N1904 has no be verb or being participle there.

13:26.sourceText: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλαις μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης.
13:26.targetText: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with much power and glory,

13:27.sourceText: καὶ τότε ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἐπισυνάξει τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρου γῆς ἕως ἄκρου οὐρανοῦ.
13:27.targetText: and then He will send His messengers, and gather together His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.

13:28.sourceText: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς ἁπαλὸς γένηται καὶ ἐκφύῃ τὰ φύλλα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·

13:34.sourceText: ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀπόδημος ἀφεὶς τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ δοὺς τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐξουσίαν, ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῷ θυρωρῷ ἐνετείλατο ἵνα γρηγορῇ.
